channel.title: OnlyBills articles
channel.description: Splitting the bill, tipping and money with friends.

item.title: Buying rounds in a UK pub: the etiquette
item.description: How rounds work in a UK pub, the unwritten rules, what to do when someone skips their round or drinks pricier drinks, and when a tab or split is fairer.

item.title: Corkage and cakeage fees: costs and how to split them
item.description: Corkage is a per bottle fee for bringing your own wine, cakeage a per head fee for your own cake. Typical UK costs, and how to split them when only some had it.

item.title: Cover charges in the UK: do you have to pay?
item.description: A cover charge is a fixed fee per diner. When it's legal in the UK, whether you have to pay it, if it goes to staff, and how to split it fairly on a group bill.

item.title: Graduation dinner: who pays, and how to split it
item.description: Who usually pays for a UK graduation meal, whether the graduate should, and how to split it fairly when two families share a table. With £ examples.

item.title: Group booking deposits: who pays and how to split them
item.description: Who pays a restaurant deposit for a group, how it comes off the bill, what happens when someone drops out, and whether no-show fees are legal in the UK.

item.title: How long does a bank transfer take in the UK?
item.description: Faster Payments usually land almost immediately, but can take up to two hours. Why some are held, and the quickest way to pay a friend back after dinner.

item.title: How to avoid an awkward bill split
item.description: Most awkward bill splits are decided before anyone orders. What to say before the meal, at the table and afterwards, with messages you can copy and a £ example.

item.title: How to pay a friend back without their bank details
item.description: Ask for their payment link, send a claim link from your bank, use PayPal or pay cash. What each way needs from you, plus limits, speed and safety checks.

item.title: How to say you only want to pay for what you had
item.description: On a budget, eating light or saving up? Why paying for what you had isn't rude, when to mention it, and word for word lines for the group chat and the table.

item.title: How to send the bill to the group chat
item.description: What to send after a group meal, when to send it, messages you can copy, what a shared bill link looks like in iMessage and how to chase gently if nobody pays.

item.title: How to split a bill when some pay cash and some pay card
item.description: Some friends have cash, some only cards. How to settle one bill so nobody loses out: who takes the cash, the change, card minimums and a worked £ example.

item.title: How to split a bill with a discount or voucher
item.description: Who gets the saving when a group bill has a voucher, 2 for 1 deal or dining card discount, and how to share it fairly, with worked £ examples to the penny.

item.title: How to split a bottomless brunch bill fairly
item.description: How to split a bottomless brunch when some take the drinks package and some don't, plus time limits, service charge and deposits. With a worked £ example.

item.title: How to split the bill when there are couples
item.description: Per couple or per head? How to split a group bill fairly when couples and singles eat together and couples drink more, plus what to say. With a £ example.

item.title: Is it safe to share your bank details with friends?
item.description: Usually, yes. What someone can and can't do with your sort code, how name checks and scam refunds work, and how to tell if a payment link is genuine.

item.title: The best bill splitting apps in the UK (2026)
item.description: Splitwise, Tricount, Settle Up, your bank's split button and OnlyBills compared: who each suits, what's free, sign-up and Android, checked November 2026.

item.title: Tricount alternatives: which app fits your group?
item.description: When Tricount is the right choice, and when Splitwise, Settle Up, Splid, Monzo Split or OnlyBills fits better, with UK prices checked in November 2026.

item.title: What is an App Clip on iPhone?
item.description: An App Clip is a small part of an app that opens from a QR code or link without installing anything. How they work, what they can see and how to remove them.

item.title: How to split a bill fairly
item.description: Three fair ways to split a restaurant bill (even, itemised and hybrid), when to use each, and one £159.19 dinner for four worked out all three ways.

item.title: How to split the bill at a restaurant
item.description: What to do at the table, from agreeing the split before you order to asking for the bill, one card or several, and getting everyone to pay back that night.

item.title: Can you ask a restaurant to split the bill?
item.description: Yes, most UK restaurants will split a bill. How staff feel about it, how to ask so it's easy for them, and when one card and settling up is kinder.

item.title: How to split the bill at a Christmas party
item.description: Deposits, pre-orders, drinks packages, service charge and dropouts. How to organise and split a Christmas party or festive meal fairly, with a worked £ example.

item.title: Leaving drinks: who pays?
item.description: Who pays at leaving drinks: the person leaving, the boss or everyone? How to handle rounds, tabs, the boss's card and a leaving meal, with £ examples.

item.title: Nobody carries cash any more. So who pays?
item.description: Cash was 8% of UK payments in 2025, down from 45% in 2015. What that did to splitting the bill, and what replaced the pile of notes on the table.

item.title: The cost of going out in the UK, and how to spend less
item.description: Half of Brits have turned down an invitation because of the cost, 63% in London. What going out costs now, and practical ways to socialise for less.

item.title: Who gets the tip? The UK tipping law explained
item.description: Since October 2024, tips and service charges must go to staff in full. Cash vs card tips, the code of practice now, and how to tip so staff get it.

item.title: How to split costs on student nights out
item.description: Pres, rounds, Ubers home and cheap dinners. Fair ways for students to split the costs of a night out on a tight budget, with £ examples and messages to copy.

item.title: Should you tip on top of a service charge?
item.description: No, not in the UK. A service charge is the tip, and by law it has to go to staff. When an extra tip makes sense, and the card machine prompt to watch out for.

item.title: What does going Dutch mean?
item.description: Going Dutch means each person pays for themselves. Where the phrase really comes from (America, not the 17th century), how Brits use it and related terms.

item.title: Pay your share without downloading an app
item.description: How web links, App Clips and bank payment links let friends join a split and pay you back with no new app or account, and what each one can see about you.
